items.title: Houthi statement from Sanaa claims three operations against Saudi Arabia with ballistic and cruise missiles and drones. King Khalid Airport in Riyadh was hit and air traffic disrupted. The Aramco refinery in Rabigh was hit and set on fire. Abha Airport, the Khamis Mushait airbase, the Aqeefah camp in Asir and sites in Najran and Jizan were also hit. The Houthis say the attacks answer 60 Saudi airstrikes on Sanaa, Al-Jawf, Taiz, Hodeidah, Saada and Marib in the past 24 hours. Airlines were warned to halt flights through Saudi airspace, with Mecca and Medina excluded.

items.title: Yemen government taking control of the bab el mandab
items.summary:
Yemen government taking control of the bab el mandab
Open Source Intel (@Osint613)
UPDATED YEMEN MAP: Operation Yemen Dawn, October 5
Major movement along Yemen’s western coast today.
Yemeni government forces captured Dhubab Airport and Al Omari Base. Fighting has now reached Mokha, according to Al Arabiya. The Dhubab to Mokha road has been cut, with Houthi forces reportedly surrounded in Dhubab.
The Houthis are advancing around Taiz, capturing Al Turbah and pushing toward Al Nashma, threatening the Taiz to Aden route.
Government forces are also advancing in Marib and Al Jawf under heavy Saudi air cover, with around 100 aircraft reportedly involved in operations.
Mokha is now a key battlefield. Its loss would threaten the Houthis’ remaining position along the southern Red Sea coast and Bab el Mandeb.
Legend:
🟦 Yemeni government forces
🟥 Houthi forces
🟧 Contested
➡️ Government and Houthi advances
✈️ Saudi airstrikes
💥 Active battlefield
Source: OSINT613 monitoring
— http://shitter.thepixora.com/Osint613/status/2107148828239401432#m

items.title: RT by @DefMon3: "The first word brigade and corps commanders use to describe the first few months of Drapatyi's tenure is 'freedom'. Unlike his predecessor, who would tell some brigade commanders how and where to fight – even specifying the coordinates where a position should be set up – Drapatyi has chosen a different approach. He has opted to decentralize command, moving away from the 'micromanagement' that has already become widely known to the public... Ukrainska Pravda sources say the move away from hands-on management of brigades and corps has brought another change: Drapatyi no longer spends several hours every day hearing reports from all commanders, as Syrskyi did. 'Syrskyi would hear reports from everyone every day and could give specific instructions on how to respond to developments, including where troops should advance… Drapatyi doesn't do that; that's the job of the troop grouping commanders. Drapatyi focuses on strategic and systemic issues. And when commanders do speak to the commander-in-chief, he isn't interested in a standard report on 'what happened', but in statistics, analysing problems and finding solutions – in other words, what conditions need to be created for a particular commander to accomplish their mission. And that's the right approach,' a senior military officer told Ukrainska Pravda." https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/10/05/8056518/

items.title: "Mr. Shmyhal, the people said, described the document as an intercepted Russian plan to cause the energy system to collapse through methodical attacks. The plan, a copy of which The New York Times obtained, describes a campaign of strikes using up to 1,000 missiles, drones and bombs. They would target a wide range of facilities, including electrical substations, hydroelectric and thermal power plants, and boiler houses. Most alarming, the document says that Russia intends to force Ukraine’s three operating nuclear plants — the backbone of its power infrastructure — to shut down by firing missiles at the electrical switchyards that connect them to the grid. The switchyards sit less than a mile from the reactors. The plan also says that Moscow will target Ukraine’s water system, including pumping stations and wastewater treatment facilities, with dozens of ballistic missiles and glide bombs. Russia has never attacked such sites on a large scale before. Ukrainian officials have privately expressed concern that the country has limited backup plans should it face severe water disruptions. The ultimate goal is to cut off major Ukrainian cities from power, heat and water, which could set off a humanitarian crisis. Kyiv, Kharkiv and Odesa are highlighted as top targets, with plans to cut electricity supplies in those cities by 90 percent, reduce heating supplies by up to 90 percent and severely disrupt the sewage system." @ConstantMeheut https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/02/world/europe/russia-ukraine-winter.html

Flying a MiG-29 fighter jet, he carried out missile and bomb strikes against Russian occupiers along one of the front-line directions. During the mission, his aircraft was hit by an enemy missile. The pilot ejected, but tragically did not survive. Captain Marat Redvanovych Mambetov was a flight commander in the 40th Tactical Aviation Brigade "Ghost of Kyiv." We extend our deepest condolences to Marat's family and loved ones. He defended Ukraine until his very last breath. 🇺🇦 Heroes never die!

Before that, GRU Unit 29155, an assassination and sabotage unit, sent one of its operatives to infiltrate Garry’s Free Russia Forum, posing as a dissident. https://theins.press/en/politics/268886
items.summary:
Russia recruited a network of assassins, since indicted by DoJ, to target @Kasparov63 . Before that, GRU Unit 29155, an assassination and sabotage unit, sent one of its operatives to infiltrate Garry’s Free Russia Forum, posing as a dissident. theins.press/en/politics/268…
Link
The enemy within: How Russia's GRU agents blend in with human rights activists, journalists, and...
An investigation by The Insider has revealed the identities of several Kremlin agents living and working under false identities inside Russia itself. All of…
theins.press
Xavier Colás (@xaviercolas)
Hoy desvelamos en @elmundoes que Rusia lleva meses planeando matar al ajedrecista y líder disidente Garry Kasparov en Estados Unidos. elmundo.es/internacional/202… Este verano las autoridades de EEUU comunicaron al fundador de Free Russia Forum que era "objetivo" de un plan del Kremlin para matarlo y se le puso protección especial por primera vez desde que se exilió y se instaló en Nueva York en 2013, según han desvelado fuentes de su entrono.
Más avanzados estaban los planes para asesinar a Ilya Ponomarev, él único diputado ruso que votó contra la anexión de Crimea y que desde el exilio ha colaborado sobre el terreno con la defensa armada de Ucrania.
(En Vilna, dos exiliados rusos en la mirilla. Uno recibió protección cuando la red de asesinos se puso en marcha en 2024)
Un reclutado a las órdenes de Moscú filmó dos emplazamientos de una de las víctimas en EEUU, respondiendo a instrucciones precisas formuladas en clave: "medir terreno"= grabar, "construir"=matar. Cada tarea tenía un precio, pero no hubo acuerdo para la segunda.
@ElMundoInter
— http://shitter.thepixora.com/xaviercolas/status/2105217861903868240#m

items.title: "The U.S. awarded Sabena Aerospace Engineering, a Belgian company, a contract of up to some $235.5 million for maintenance of Ukraine’s F-16s, though subcontractors perform some of the work. Phase inspection generally takes two to six weeks in the U.S., but it’s 'taking as long as 40 weeks in Belgium,' says retired U.S. Navy Rear Adm. Mark Montgomery. Another Western source tells us that more than half of Ukraine’s F-16s are currently in maintenance limbo, and at the current pace of use and maintenance Kyiv will exhaust the rest by the end of the year. A Ukrainian air force spokesman declined to comment." https://www.wsj.com/opinion/ukraine-f-16-maintenance-delays-russia-sabena-engineering-85ca626a
